title: Enterprise Security FAQ (v2) — Changelog (2026)
author: Naomi Feldman
content:
## Purpose
This page tracks the **2026 version history** of the **Enterprise Security FAQ (v2)** and records what changed, why it changed, and who approved the update. This is the canonical changelog for field enablement and auditability.

- **Canonical FAQ page:** confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/enterprise-security-faq-v2
- **Field packaging (PDF):** Distributed via the “Security Enablement Kit v2” Drive folder (see internal link on the FAQ page)

## Change management rules (quick)
1. **No ad-hoc edits** directly on the FAQ page without an entry here.
2. Each version must include:
   - Summary of changes
   - Customer impact (what SE/AEs should say differently)
   - Approval record (Security Eng + GRC + Product)
3. If a change affects external references, coordinate with Docs (redwood-docs) and update the “Public-safe Security FAQ (high level)” if applicable.

## Version history (2026)
| Version | Date (PT) | Type | Summary | Primary owner | Approval record |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| v2.2 | 2026-02-24 | Patch | Clarifications based on Q1 field feedback (audit log scope wording, residency phrasing, SCIM language). No posture change. | Naomi Feldman | See **Approval: FAQ v2.2** (links below) |
| v2.1 | 2026-02-10 | Patch | Tightened incident notification language; updated retention default wording; added evidence request routing notes. | Naomi Feldman | See **Approval: FAQ v2.1** (links below) |
| v2.0 | 2026-02-03 | Major | Enterprise Security FAQ v2 published (Hosted/Dedicated/Private boundary rewrite + new one-pager references). | Naomi Feldman | See **Approval: FAQ v2.0** (links below) |
| v1.9 | 2026-01-12 | Pre-release | Internal draft baseline created for kit refresh; not for external distribution. | Naomi Feldman | Reviewed informally; superseded by v2.0 |

## v2.2 (2026-02-24) — Patch
### What changed
**Audit logging**
- Clarified that audit logging coverage is **control-plane and console/API administrative actions**; avoided implying universal coverage of all data-plane inference events.
- Added explicit note that export options depend on deployment mode (**Hosted/Dedicated/Private**) and customer SIEM setup.

**Data residency**
- Replaced ambiguous “data stays in-region” phrasing with a **mode-specific statement**:
  - Hosted: request processing region selection (where available) + logs/telemetry handling described in the residency one-pager.
  - Dedicated: dedicated regional capacity; clarified what remains in Redwood-managed systems.
  - Private: customer-managed networking boundary; clarified control plane vs data plane responsibilities.

**SSO / SCIM**
- Updated SCIM language to “supported for eligible enterprise plans; confirm tenant configuration with Solutions Engineering” (removed phrasing that read as universally available).

**Evidence pointers / how to request**
- Standardized the “How to request SOC 2 / pen test summary / subprocessor list” section to match the internal evidence process routing (no change to what can be shared; improved clarity on steps).

### Why it changed
- Addressed repeated confusion surfaced by AEs/SEs during late-stage security reviews (particularly around audit log scope and data residency wording).

### Customer-facing impact (talk track)
- Use: “We provide audit logs for key administrative actions in the Redwood Console/control plane; coverage differs by deployment mode and we can share a sample event set.”
- Use: “Residency controls and data flows are documented per mode; Dedicated/Private materially change the boundary and operational responsibilities.”

### Links

- Audit logging one-pager: confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-overview-one-pager

## v2.1 (2026-02-10) — Patch
### What changed
**Incident response / notification language**
- Reworded the notification section to avoid over-commitment and to align with contract terms:
  - Removed “within X hours” statements from the FAQ.
  - Added: “Notification timelines are **contract-dependent**; Redwood will provide timely notice consistent with applicable agreements and law.”
- Added pointer to the incident response one-pager for standardized, customer-facing detail.

**Retention defaults and deletion requests**
- Updated retention wording to reflect defaults vs configurable options (where available) and clarified that certain logs may have different retention requirements.

**RFP routing guidance**
- Added explicit guidance: questions about breach definitions, indemnity, or DPAs should route to **Legal/Finance**; evidence requests route to **GRC**.

### Why it changed
- Triggered by late-stage procurement redlines and repeated AE requests for “approved incident wording” that does not create unintended commitments.

### Customer-facing impact (talk track)
- Use: “We share our incident response approach and will notify per the terms of the agreement; we can provide our customer-facing IR one-pager.”
- Avoid: “We always notify within 24 hours” (unless explicitly contracted).

## v2.0 (2026-02-03) — Major release
### What changed
**Major restructure: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private**
- Rewrote the FAQ to clearly separate:
  - **Redwood responsibilities** vs **customer responsibilities**
  - Control plane vs data plane boundaries
  - Differences in logging, networking, and key management across modes

**Added/updated enterprise topics**
- Data residency and retention: added explicit references to dedicated one-pagers and standardized language used in RFP responses.
- Audit logging: added a precise “what is logged” section and pointed to the audit logging overview one-pager.
- SSO/SAML/RBAC: aligned terminology and role naming to the RBAC reference and SSO one-pager.
- Evidence process: added a safe, customer-facing description of how SOC 2 access works (high-level only).

**Removed/avoided**
- Roadmap commitments framed as guarantees.
- Absolute statements (e.g., “always/never”) where operational realities vary by customer configuration and deployment mode.

### Why it changed
- Enterprise security reviews were slowed by inconsistent answers across Sales/SE/Security and by older FAQ language that didn’t match current deployment options (especially **Private**).

### Customer-facing impact (talk track)
- Use: “We have a unified inference platform, but the security boundary changes meaningfully across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; the FAQ and one-pagers are structured to make that explicit.”

## How to propose a change
1. File a ticket in Linear under the enablement kit project (PM-1847/PM-1852) and include:
   - Proposed wording (old vs new)
   - Reason (customer request, product change, legal guidance)
   - Deployment modes affected (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
2. Tag required reviewers: Security Eng (Marcus Lin), GRC (Olga Petrov), Product owner for the impacted mode(s), and Solutions Eng (Markus Klein).
3. After approval:
   - Update the FAQ page
   - Add a new changelog entry here
   - If needed, trigger docs-site updates via ENG ticket (Docs team)

## Notes on distribution
- This changelog is **internal**.
- Customer-facing materials are the FAQ page content and the exported PDFs; sharing of formal evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) must follow the evidence request process documented by GRC.
